name: context_compaction
description: The conversation ran out of context and was compacted.
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

prose.cumulative_dropped_tokens: Tokens dropped CUMULATIVELY across every compaction in this session, not this one’s own drop. The name says so because the trap is real: a per-event reading of this field over-counts the cost of any session compacted more than once. `pre_tokens - post_tokens` is this event’s own drop.
prose.discovered_tools: A JSON array of tools the compaction discovered and kept available. OMITTED when the transcript does not carry it -- measured: present on 282 of 438 compactions, absent on the other 156. The absence is not an empty list; an empty array here means the compaction ran and found none, and the two are different facts. An EMPTY array is a real measurement meaning "looked and found nothing".
prose.duration_ms: How long the compaction itself took. Measured present on 438 of 438.
prose.occurred_at: When the event happened, from the transcript’s own timestamp field. NOT the envelope’s `recorded_at`, which is when ascend ingested it -- during a backfill those differ by years. Present on all 1,488 entries measured 2026-09-15, and still not `required`: a transcript without one is a real state, and omitting is how it stays distinguishable from an event at the epoch.
prose.post_tokens: Context size immediately AFTER the compaction, in tokens.
prose.pre_tokens: Context size immediately BEFORE the compaction, in tokens. Present on every compaction measured (438 of 438). Paired with `post_tokens` it is the only direct measurement of how close a session came to the limit.
prose.project: The transcript’s project directory under ~/.claude/projects, in ENCODED form ("-Users-me-src-app"), which is the name on disk. Not decoded: a "-" in that name stands for both a path separator and a literal hyphen, so decoding is lossy and two projects can collide. The encoded name never does. This is a COARSE label by construction -- one per project, however many directories the work happened in. For the real working directory, select the envelope’s `cwd` column, which this type’s generated view already projects and which is populated from the transcript’s own record.
prose.session_id: The transcript’s own session id. Half of this entry’s identity, so it is required: without it the entry has no stable key and re-running an ingest could not recognise it, so the adapter emits nothing rather than an unkeyable entry.
prose.trigger: What caused the compaction, as the transcript records it. Deliberately a string rather than an enum: this vocabulary belongs to Claude Code, so a closed list would turn the next new value into a rejected entry rather than a recorded one.

name: decision
description: A choice between alternatives that were both genuinely viable.
record_when: a choice is made between approaches that were both real options -- the kind worth reopening later. Not every choice: if there was only one reasonable thing to do, it was not a decision, and recording it as one makes the entries that matter harder to find.
purpose: Keep the choices worth reopening, with what was rejected and why.
analysis_questions: Was reversibility marked correctly on the ones that were?

prose.chosen: The option that was taken, spelled as it appears in `options_considered` so the two can be matched without guessing at paraphrase.
prose.options_considered: A JSON array, one entry per alternative that was actually on the table. Each entry is a string naming the option, or an object with `option` plus `pros` and `cons`. Writing the pros and cons is what makes this worth recording -- a list of names with no reasoning is reconstructable from the diff. An EMPTY array is a real measurement meaning "looked and found nothing" -- leave the property out entirely to say nobody looked.
prose.rationale: Why that one and not the others. This is the part that cannot be recovered from the resulting code, which records what was chosen and never what was rejected.
prose.reversibility: What it would cost to change this later. An `irreversible` choice is the one a later reader most needs the reasoning for, so this is what makes the rationale findable.

name: evidence_record
description: One EV-protocol measurement: a question asked before anything ran, what was run to answer it, the raw numbers, and what was decided.
record_when: you finish a measurement taken to answer a question you named before running anything -- a benchmark, a comparison, a spike, a kappa or interval computation, an A/B of two approaches. Record it once the numbers are in and a decision follows from them, not while still iterating. Copy `measurement` verbatim, exact text, as the tool printed it -- a paraphrase of a number is a new number, and only the exact text is what a later search or re-check can match against.
purpose: Keep measured answers to questions named before measuring.
analysis_questions: How often did a result contradict its pre-registered prediction?

prose.arms: A JSON object or array, one entry per arm compared, each carrying its own count and n -- for example `{"a": {"count": 3, "n": 40}, "b": {"count": 11, "n": 40}}`. The point is to make the losing arm a queryable field rather than a sentence buried in `measurement`'s prose, so a later query can pull every record where a named arm lost without re-reading the text. An EMPTY array is a real measurement meaning "looked and found nothing" -- leave the property out entirely to say nobody looked.
prose.bead: The task this record belongs to, e.g. `asc-c9h`. Grouping records by this field is how a later reader assembles everything measured for one piece of work without re-reading every entry.
prose.confidence: What this measurement does NOT establish -- its sample size, its scope, what a different input might change. This is required in the sense that the omission must be a DECISION, not silence: if there is truly nothing to caveat, say that plainly ("n is large enough that this generalizes", "no known limitation") rather than leaving the property out or inventing a limitation that was not actually considered.
prose.decision: What was chosen, and the threshold that decided it. Name the specific cutoff or comparison that made this outcome win -- 'it looked better' is not a threshold, and without one the decision cannot be checked against a different measurement later.
prose.measured_on: When the measurement was actually taken, if that differs from when this entry was written. The envelope's own `recorded_at` is when the ENTRY was written, which can trail the measurement by however long it took to write it up -- leave this out when the two coincide.
prose.measurement: The numbers, raw, with n. Exact text, as printed by whatever produced them -- not a summary, not a rounded restatement. A number without the sample size it came from is not a measurement a later reader can trust.
prose.method: What was run, against what data, and how many times. Name the tool or script, the input it ran over, and the repeat count -- a method that does not say how many times something ran cannot be told apart from a single lucky sample.
prose.question: The question, named BEFORE anything was run. Write it as it was asked at the start, not as it reads now that the answer is known -- a question restated in light of its own answer stops being a question and becomes a justification.

name: note
description: A correction to an earlier entry, or a finding that fits no other registered type.
record_when: you need to correct something an earlier entry got wrong, or you have something worth recording that does not match any other type's shape. `note` is the type of last resort: reach for a more specific type first, and use `note` only when none fits -- a corpus where everything is a `note` is a corpus where nothing can be queried by shape.
purpose: The last-resort type, for what fits no other shape.
analysis_questions: What share of notes should have been another type?

prose.text: The correction or finding, in prose. State plainly what it corrects if it corrects something -- naming the entry or claim being corrected is what makes this findable later instead of just another unattached sentence.

name: review_completed
description: A review of some work reached a verdict.
record_when: a review finishes at any stage -- a code review, a review of a plan or a design, or a self-review before handing work off. Record it when you reach a verdict, not while you are still reading: a review with no verdict is not yet an entry, and an entry recorded mid-review is a claim you may have to contradict.
analysis_questions: What share of reviews end in changes requested?

prose.findings: A JSON array, one object per problem found: `severity` (one of critical, high, medium, low), `category` (one of bug, security, design, style, docs, test), `file` for the path it is in, and `note` for anything that does not fit the other three. An EMPTY array is a real measurement meaning "looked and found nothing" -- leave the property out entirely to say nobody looked.
prose.stage: What the review covered, in the words the plan uses, so it joins `stage_transition`'s `stage`. A string rather than an enum because stage names are the project's own.
prose.verdict: `approved` -- good to proceed. `changes_requested` -- the approach holds, fix these and continue. `rejected` -- the approach itself is wrong, and fixing the findings would not save it. The distinction between the last two is the one worth being careful about.

name: review_finding
description: One finding an adversarial reviewer reported, derived from the reviewer’s own report rather than from anything it chose to run. MEASURED 2026-09-26: this type has ZERO entries, and that is the state it ships in -- the tool it derives from (`ReportFindings`) exists in the harness and was called 0 times across 1,236 transcript files and 637,258 records. A derived type with no producer is not a broken one, but it is not a useful one either, and the honest place to say so is here rather than in a report that shows a clean zero. When the first reviewer reports, this fills with no change to this file. THE ONE CLOSED VOCABULARY WE DO NOT OWN is `class` -- see `FINDING_LENSES` for the provenance, the reason, and the version-bump cost of a tenth lens. `catchable_by` IS DECLARED AND NEVER FILLED: nothing in the harness report carries it, so it is absent on every entry rather than empty on some, and an absent judgment field is `not_measured` -- the default, needing no encoding at all. It is declared because its absence is then a stated expectation instead of an oversight, and because the handler that asks the question names it under `judged` (asc-6ola.9).
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

prose.catchable_by: What would have caught this before it shipped -- a test, a check, a type. ALWAYS ABSENT TODAY, and that is not an oversight: nothing in the reviewer’s report carries it, so the deriver never sets it and no entry has ever had a value. It is declared so that an absent `catchable_by` reads as `not_measured` on a field the type expects, which is a different fact from a field nobody thought of. It exists for the question `asc-gtnu` is actually asking -- whether the implementer later ran a check that would have caught it -- and that question is unanswerable in both directions until this has values. Note that the SAME gap exists on the other side of the join: `check.run` carries no path, so "did a check run on THIS file" is not derivable either (spike/review-join/FINDINGS.md).
prose.class: Which lens found this, as one of the nine slugs in `FINDING_LENSES`. THIS IS AN ENUM ON PURPOSE, and it is the only place in ascend where a vocabulary we do not own is closed -- the reason is that comparable counts by class are the entire product of this type, and an open string gives nine spellings of one lens. A tenth lens needs a type version bump, and a value outside the nine is REFUSED here with the allowed values printed; the normalizer counts that refusal so the fact is not lost with the entry. Deliberately NOT the same axis as `review_completed.findings[].category`, which is what KIND of problem this is rather than how the reviewer looked.
prose.failure_scenario: Concrete inputs or state leading to a wrong outcome, in the reviewer’s words. This is the field that separates a real finding from a suspicion, and it is the one a later reader needs in order to check the claim rather than trust it -- so it is carried verbatim as the reviewer wrote it, never summarized.
prose.file: The file the finding is in, as the reviewer’s report gives it -- repo-relative, not resolved against anything here. Required: a finding with no file is a finding about the design rather than the code, and it would join nothing, which is the one thing this type exists to do. Measured on the corpus: this path is the JOIN KEY between a reviewer’s finding and the implementer’s `file.changed` events for the same file, and a measured 58.1% of that join crosses streams within one session (spike/review-join/FINDINGS.md).
prose.line: The line the finding is anchored to. OMITTED when the reviewer’s report carries no line, which is an ordinary state -- a finding about a missing guard or an unhandled error path often has no single line. Omitted rather than `0`, because line 0 is not a place in a file and a reader who sees it would have to guess which was meant.
prose.occurred_at: When the event happened, from the transcript’s own timestamp field. NOT the envelope’s `recorded_at`, which is when ascend ingested it -- during a backfill those differ by years. Present on all 1,488 entries measured 2026-09-15, and still not `required`: a transcript without one is a real state, and omitting is how it stays distinguishable from an event at the epoch.
prose.project: The transcript’s project directory under ~/.claude/projects, in ENCODED form ("-Users-me-src-app"), which is the name on disk. Not decoded: a "-" in that name stands for both a path separator and a literal hyphen, so decoding is lossy and two projects can collide. The encoded name never does. This is a COARSE label by construction -- one per project, however many directories the work happened in. For the real working directory, select the envelope’s `cwd` column, which this type’s generated view already projects and which is populated from the transcript’s own record.
prose.reviewer_model: The model that produced the finding, from the stream’s own `model.context`. NOT an enum, for the reason measured there: one model is spelled `deepseek-v4.1-flash` on one field and `deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud` on another, so a closed list would be wrong before it was written. It is what makes "which model’s findings survive review" a stratified question rather than a pooled one. OMITTED when the transcript names no model for the stream.
prose.session_id: The transcript’s own session id. Half of this entry’s identity, so it is required: without it the entry has no stable key and re-running an ingest could not recognise it, so the adapter emits nothing rather than an unkeyable entry.
prose.summary: The finding in the reviewer’s own words, one sentence. Required because it is the only field that says what is actually wrong: the class says where to look next and the file says where, and neither says what.
prose.tool_use_id: The reviewer’s report call this finding came from -- a `ReportFindings` tool_use id from the transcript. Required, and it is the identity: one report call carries an ARRAY of findings, so the key is this id plus the finding’s position in that array, and a re-derivation finds the same entries rather than appending duplicates. The position is not a property because the key already carries it, the way `context_compaction` keeps its record uuid in the key rather than in a field.
prose.verdict: The reviewer’s own confidence in the finding. Measured values: `CONFIRMED`, `PLAUSIBLE`. A string and NOT an enum, and that is the rule above applied rather than an exception to it: this vocabulary belongs to the harness’s report format, not to ascend, so closing it would turn a third verdict value into a rejected entry the day the harness adds one. Deliberately a string rather than an enum: this vocabulary belongs to Claude Code, so a closed list would turn the next new value into a rejected entry rather than a recorded one.

All 33 reported calls are in EPHEMERAL probe projects, which ingest skips by design, so the reported route has still not fired on real work -- that is the gap the `on_skill` nudge (`handlers/review-finding-nudge.yaml`) exists to close, by asking a reviewer for `ReportFindings` at the moment it loads the review skill. The superseded sentence was a dated measurement rather than an error, and it is recorded here because a type description is a measurement with a date on it, and the date is how a later reader knows which one to trust (dogfood/0021). This is the field that separates a real finding from a suspicion, and it is the one a later reader needs in order to check the claim rather than trust it -- so it is carried verbatim as the reviewer wrote it, never summarized. name: search_miss
description: A search that returned an answer we acted on, or nearly acted on, that was not the answer to the question we asked.
record_when: a search misleads you -- a grep, rg, glob, FTS query or `asc query` whose result you read as an answer and which was not one. Record it at the moment you find out, and record it EVEN IF you caught it before acting, because the near-misses are the ones that measure how often the instrument lies rather than how often you were lucky. The countable question this type exists to answer is 'how often does our searching mislead us, and in which way', so `failure_mode` and `caught` are the two fields that must be right. NOT for a search that simply found nothing when nothing was there -- that is a correct answer, and recording it drowns the ones that matter. The test is whether the RESULT supported a conclusion the evidence did not: a zero read as 'does not exist' qualifies, a zero read as 'zero' does not.
purpose: Measure how often this project’s searches mislead it, and in which way.
analysis_questions: What share were caught before_acting rather than after a wrong claim?

prose.caught: When it was noticed. This is the field that turns the type into a measurement rather than a diary: `before_acting` counts near-misses, `after_wrong_claim` counts times a false statement was actually made and then retracted. A corpus of only `before_acting` entries is a corpus that is not recording its real failures.
prose.command: The full invocation, including flags and redirections. `grep -c` and `grep -o` fail in different ways and the flags are usually where the failure lives -- `-c` counts LINES not matches, `-o` changes what a count means, and a compound `-e a -e b` reports that something matched without saying what.
prose.corrected_by: The search or check that produced the real answer, verbatim, so the entry carries the remedy and not only the fault. Where the fix was a different KIND of evidence rather than a better pattern -- reading a file, a token count, an experiment -- say that instead.
prose.expected: What the searcher expected the result to mean, written as the claim they were about to make. Not 'I expected matches' -- 'I expected a match to prove the hook fired'. Without this the entry cannot show why the result was misleading, only what it was.
prose.failure_mode: How it misled. `compound_pattern`: several alternates in one search, so a hit does not say which matched. `wrong_vocabulary`: the pattern was guessed from the wrong output format or schema, so it could never have matched. `wrong_scope`: the pattern matched in a region where a match does not support the claim. `absence_wrongly_trusted`: zero results read as 'does not exist'. `overmatch`: matched far more than intended and the excess was not noticed. `tool_error`: the search itself errored and the error was stepped over rather than read. `flag_semantics`: the flags meant something other than what the searcher assumed.
prose.pattern: The pattern as it was actually written, verbatim and unescaped-as-typed. Not a description of it. The whole value of this entry to a later reader is being able to see the literal string that misled someone, and a paraphrase of a pattern is a different pattern.
prose.returned: What came back, exact text as printed, including a count or an error message. A paraphrase of a number is a new number.
prose.scope: What was searched -- paths, globs, or the region of a file. Scope is a failure mode in its own right: a pattern can be correct and still answer the wrong question because the haystack contained a region where a match means something else.
prose.search_tool: Which instrument. Named `search_tool` rather than `tool` because the corpus already holds `tool_name` on derived entries, where it means a Claude Code tool such as Bash or Read -- a different kind of thing, and the drift guard was right to flag the collision. Kept as a field rather than baked into the type name so that 'how often does grep mislead us' is a WHERE clause and not a separate type: the failure modes are shared across instruments, and splitting by tool would split the counts that make them visible.
prose.wrong_conclusion: The claim that was actually made or nearly made on this evidence, in the words it was stated in. Omit when nothing was concluded -- never write 'none' or an empty string, which are indistinguishable from an unfilled field.

name: skill_activation
description: A skill became active and stayed active.
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

name: stage_transition
description: A stage of a written plan changed status.
record_when: a stage in a plan document changes status -- the plan is the trigger, so record the transition when you edit that line, not at the end of the session when you no longer remember what was true at the moment it flipped.
purpose: See how plans actually move between stages.
analysis_questions: How often does a stage go complete without its tests passing?

prose.from_status: The status it had. One of the three the plan format allows.
prose.stage: The stage as the plan names it, including its number -- "Stage 2: the store". Matching `review_completed`'s `stage` makes "what was reviewed while this stage was open" a join rather than a guess.
prose.tests_passing: Whether the whole gate was green at the moment of the transition. Omit it if the gate was not run -- "the tests were failing" and "nobody ran the tests" are different facts, and `false` asserts the first.
prose.to_status: The status it now has. Equal to `from_status` is legal and usually a mistake -- record the transition, not the state.

name: stuck_event
description: A problem resisted repeated attempts and forced a stop.
record_when: the three-strike rule fires -- three attempts at the same problem have failed and you are stopping to reassess rather than trying a fourth variation. Record it at the moment you stop, not after you recover: the value of this entry is the state of mind you are about to leave, and it is the least reconstructable thing in the whole store. Keep the failing output as it was printed while you still have it -- `error_text` wants the exact words, and only the exact words are what a later search can find.
purpose: Find where three attempts at one problem fail, while the state of mind is still recoverable.
analysis_questions: Do stuck events cluster by area of the code, or by kind of error?

prose.attempt_count: How many attempts were made before stopping. This is the count of attempts MADE, which may exceed the length of `what_was_tried` -- some attempts are not worth writing down.
prose.error_text: The failure as it was printed, verbatim. Not a summary -- the exact text is what makes this findable by a later search, and a paraphrase destroys the only part a search matches.
prose.hypothesis: What you believe is actually wrong, stated as a belief rather than a finding. The point is to record the guess that the next attempt was about to test.
prose.resolution: How it ended: `fixed` (the real cause was found), `worked_around` (the symptom is gone and the cause remains), `escalated` (handed to someone or something else), `abandoned` (the goal was dropped), `unresolved` (stopped without a fix and not coming back). Leave `resolution` out ENTIRELY if the problem is still open -- that is a different claim from `unresolved`, which means you stopped for good.
prose.what_was_tried: A JSON array of what was attempted, in the order tried -- either bare strings, or objects with `attempt` and `result`. Order is the point: the sequence is how a later reader sees which ideas have already been spent. An EMPTY array is a real measurement meaning "looked and found nothing" -- leave the property out entirely to say nobody looked.

name: tool_denial
description: A tool call was refused before it ran.
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

prose.denial_kind: Why it was refused. Measured values, 2026-09-15: `permission-rule` (228), `user-rejected` (160), `automode-unavailable` (39), `automode-blocked` (30). The distinction that matters is user-rejected versus the rest: that one is a judgement someone made about this work, and the others are configuration. Deliberately a string rather than an enum: this vocabulary belongs to Claude Code, so a closed list would turn the next new value into a rejected entry rather than a recorded one.
prose.occurred_at: When the event happened, from the transcript’s own timestamp field. NOT the envelope’s `recorded_at`, which is when ascend ingested it -- during a backfill those differ by years. Present on all 1,488 entries measured 2026-09-15, and still not `required`: a transcript without one is a real state, and omitting is how it stays distinguishable from an event at the epoch.
prose.project: The transcript’s project directory under ~/.claude/projects, in ENCODED form ("-Users-me-src-app"), which is the name on disk. Not decoded: a "-" in that name stands for both a path separator and a literal hyphen, so decoding is lossy and two projects can collide. The encoded name never does. This is a COARSE label by construction -- one per project, however many directories the work happened in. For the real working directory, select the envelope’s `cwd` column, which this type’s generated view already projects and which is populated from the transcript’s own record.
prose.session_id: The transcript’s own session id. Half of this entry’s identity, so it is required: without it the entry has no stable key and re-running an ingest could not recognise it, so the adapter emits nothing rather than an unkeyable entry.
prose.tool_name: The tool that was refused, resolved by joining the denial back to the `tool_use` block that invoked it. Measured: resolved on 457 of 457 denials, so in practice it is always here -- but it is not `required`, because the join depends on a per-file map and a transcript split across a rotation would break it. Omitted rather than guessed.
prose.tool_use_id: The refused invocation’s own id from the transcript. Unique within a session and paired with `session_id` to key the entry. Measured: 454 distinct ids over 457 denials, and the three repeats are in DIFFERENT sessions, so the pair is unique where the id alone is not.

name: user_correction
description: The user pushed back on what was being done. Every entry of this type also carries a tool_denial for the same event -- measured, 20 of 20 -- so this is NOT an independent corpus: a count over corrections must not be corroborated by a count over denials, because they are the same events. It is kept for `evidence_text`, which holds what the user actually said and which no other type records.
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

For the real working directory, select the envelope’s `cwd` column, which this type’s generated view already projects and which is populated from the transcript’s own record.

prose.tool_name: The tool being called when the correction arrived, resolved like `tool_denial`’s. Measured: resolvable on all 20 corrections.

name: verification_run
description: A check command was run and the gate changed state. NOT every check invocation: the adapter records a run that produced a verdict CHANGE, or the first verified pass in a transcript. Measured: 6,826 commands in the corpus run a check, and 486 entries survive the filter. Without it every `pnpm test` would be a row, and a red-green loop would fill the store with its own keystrokes.
record_when: Never by hand -- asc ingest claude-code derives one from each transcript.

prose.occurred_at: When the event happened, from the transcript’s own timestamp field. NOT the envelope’s `recorded_at`, which is when ascend ingested it -- during a backfill those differ by years. Present on all 1,488 entries measured 2026-09-15, and still not `required`: a transcript without one is a real state, and omitting is how it stays distinguishable from an event at the epoch.
prose.previous_verdict: The verdict of the PREVIOUS check run in the same session, when there was one. OMITTED on a first verified pass, where there is no previous run -- which is a different fact from a run that repeated an earlier verdict, and the reason this type can answer "what was red just before it went green" with no joins.
prose.project: The transcript’s project directory under ~/.claude/projects, in ENCODED form ("-Users-me-src-app"), which is the name on disk. Not decoded: a "-" in that name stands for both a path separator and a literal hyphen, so decoding is lossy and two projects can collide. The encoded name never does. This is a COARSE label by construction -- one per project, however many directories the work happened in. For the real working directory, select the envelope’s `cwd` column, which this type’s generated view already projects and which is populated from the transcript’s own record.
prose.runner: The check that ran, reduced to its execution head and first argument -- `pnpm test`, `cargo test`, `npx vitest`. NOT the full command: a Bash command can be a heredoc holding an entire file, and storing one would put transcript prose in the store by the back door. Truncated to 60 characters.
prose.session_id: The transcript’s own session id. Half of this entry’s identity, so it is required: without it the entry has no stable key and re-running an ingest could not recognise it, so the adapter emits nothing rather than an unkeyable entry.
prose.verdict: Whether the run passed, from the tool result’s own `is_error` field rather than from anything in the output text. Measured: `is_error` was a boolean on every check result seen, so this is never inferred from prose. A result without one yields no entry at all rather than a guessed verdict.

prose.verdict: Whether the run passed. Read from the tool result’s `is_error` only when that exit status is the check’s own -- nothing after the check but `&&`. Otherwise from a summary line in the output (`verdict_source`), because `pnpm test | tail` exits 0 on a failing suite: measured, `is_error` said passed over 1,236 runs whose own output said failed. A run where neither settles it yields no entry at all.
prose.verdict_source: Where `verdict` was read. `exit_status`: the tool result’s `is_error`, which was the check’s own. `output`: a summary line the check printed, used when something after the check could replace its exit status. An output pass needs a line that speaks for the whole run (vitest’s `Test Files`, align’s `verdict:`); a failure needs any failure line, because filtering output can hide one but never invent one.
